questions.statement: Which word means the part of the body you use to hear?

options.feedback: 'Eye' is used for seeing, not for hearing.
'Mouth' is used for eating and speaking.
'Ear' is the organ used for hearing.
'Hand' is used for touching and holding objects.

questions.explanation:
'Ear' es el organo de la audicion; 'eye' se usa para ver. Esta forma se practica tambien con los otros verbos de la misma serie.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'She has long ____ and she brushes them every night.'

options.feedback: 'Hand' would take 'it' in the singular, not 'them'.
'Foot' does not match the plural pronoun 'them' used here.
'Hair' is brushed daily and takes the plural pronoun 'them' in this loose sense.
'Leg' would normally take 'his' or 'her legs', not 'them'.

questions.explanation:
Lo que se cepilla todas las noches es el pelo, y el pronombre 'them' confirma que es plural.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which word means the part you use to walk?

options.feedback: 'Knee' bends the leg but does not touch the ground when walking.
'Shoulder' is in the upper body and does not help walking directly.
'Toe' is part of the foot but is not the main organ used to walk.
'Foot' is the part that supports walking and running.

questions.explanation:
'Foot' y 'leg' forman parte del aparato locomotor; 'foot' es el que se apoya al caminar.

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'He hurt his finger while cooking.' What does 'his' refer to?

options.feedback: 'His' cannot refer to a body part in this construction.
The possessive 'his' agrees with the male subject 'he'.
The possessive does not point to a place.
'His' refers to a person, not to an activity.

questions.explanation:
'His' se refiere a 'he', el sujeto de la oracion. El mismo criterio se aplica al resto del vocabulario del tema.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct word: 'I brush my ____ twice a day.'

options.feedback: 'Teeth' is the regular plural of 'tooth' and fits 'my' before it.
The regular plural of 'tooth' is 'teeth', never 'teeths'.
That plural form does not exist in English.
'My tooth' would refer to a single tooth, which 'twice a day' contradicts.

questions.explanation:
Las acciones de cepillado se aplican a los dientes, y el articulo 'my' concuerda en singular.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Sintaxis con partes del cuerpo, grado 3.

options.text: My brother don't like his new shoes.
options.feedback: 'Do not' cannot agree with the singular 'brother'.

options.text: My brother does not like his new shoes.
options.feedback: 'Does not' goes with the third person singular 'brother'.

options.text: My brother not like his new shoes.
options.feedback: The auxiliary 'does' is missing before 'not'.

options.text: My brother does not likes his new shoes.
options.feedback: After 'does not' the verb must be in the base form 'like'.

questions.explanation:
En la forma negativa se usa 'do not' o 'does not' segun el sujeto, con el verbo en forma base.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What do you use to hold a pencil?
questions.context: Vocabulario del cuerpo en accion, grado 3.

options.feedback: 'Head' carries thoughts; it does not hold a pencil.
'Back' supports the body, not a pencil.
'Chin' is part of the face and plays no role in holding objects.
'Hand' is the body part used to grip and hold objects.

questions.explanation:
'Hand' es la parte del cuerpo que sostiene un lapiz u otro objeto pequeno. Esta estructura se repite con otros sustantivos del mismo grupo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The pupils of my eyes are ____ in bright light.'
questions.context: Descripcion de partes del cuerpo, grado 3.

options.feedback: Bright light makes the pupil contract, so it becomes small.
In darkness the pupil dilates and becomes bigger.
'Black' describes the colour of the pupil, not its size in this sentence.
'Long' does not apply to the pupil, which is round.

questions.explanation:
La pupila se contrae con la luz intensa, de modo que 'small' es el adjetivo correcto.
